title: Scaling an image
description:
Resize a pixel buffer with nearest-neighbour and with bilinear filtering.

```
4x4 checkerboard -> 8x8 nearest: sharp squares
4x4 gradient -> 8x8 bilinear: smooth steps
2x2 -> 1x1 bilinear: the average of the four
```
hints: The source position of target pixel `x` is `(x + 0.5f) * src.w / w - 0.5f` (lesson 4.04).
Bilinear: blend left and right by the fraction of x, do the same on the row below, then blend the two rows by the fraction of y.
requirements: Images are width, height and a `std::vector<std::uint8_t>` of grey values.
Nearest picks the source pixel under each target pixel's centre.
Bilinear blends the four nearest source pixels, clamping at the edges.
stretch: Do the same through WIC with `IWICBitmapScaler` and compare.
